message.content: {"edits":[{"op":"set_pin","component":"M1","pin":"Drain","net":"net2","why":"The drain joins the diode-connected mirror node that feeds the gates of M15 and M16"},{"op":"merge_nets","nets":["net10","net12"],"why":"The source of the pipeline's M10 shares a node with the M14 drain, the M9 drain and the M15 drain, so it is not dangling"},{"op":"set_pin","component":"R1","pin":"Neg","net":"bias","why":"The bottom of R1 goes to the drain of the diode-connected bias transistor, not to ground"},{"op":"set_pin","component":"M13","pin":"Drain","net":"bias"},{"op":"set_pin","component":"M13","pin":"Gate","net":"bias"},{"op":"set_pin","component":"M14","pin":"Gate","net":"bias","why":"The gate is on the bias net; the drain is the separate net14"},{"op":"set_pin","component":"M14","pin":"Source","net":"GND"},{"op":"set_pin","component":"M15","pin":"Gate","net":"bias","why":"The bottom bias line runs to the M6/M7 gates and hops over the ground leads"},{"op":"set_pin","component":"M15","pin":"Source","net":"GND"},{"op":"set_pin","component":"M16","pin":"Gate","net":"bias"},{"op":"set_pin","component":"C1","pin":"Neg","net":"GND","why":"The capacitor bottom goes to a ground symbol"}]}

The M1 gate also traces back to that same vertical line at x=200, which confirms net2 for both. So the pipeline's drain assignment for M1 should be changed to net2.

I'm matching the pipeline's M8 to the image's M2, the input PMOS near x 300–340, and I'm checking whether the drain net and gate net assignments hold up for that device.

Now I'm mapping the pipeline's M10 NMOS onto the image's M4, where the drain goes to net7 and the source sits at net12. I'm tracing where the M4 source connects, down to a node near y=315 that also reaches M14's drain and the M6 drain, and checking whether M2's drain runs into that same net.

I'm tracing the pipeline's M10 NMOS against the image's M4, and I need its source to tie into the node where M6's drain meets the wire from M14. The wires near x=576 are hard to read, since some lines end in dots and others seem to cross, so I'm checking which ones actually connect.

I'm comparing the pipeline's M10 with the image's M4, and the M14 drain and gate both appear to land on the same net10 node near y=315. The M3 drain and the M6 drain seem to meet at that node too, though the wires near x=576 are hard to separate.

I'm tracing the M4 and M5 gates, which look tied together at x=654, and checking whether that node runs down to the M4 source net that the pipeline lists as net12.

I'm checking how the wire at x=576 connects the M4 source to the M6 drain and the M3 drain, since the dots and hops there are hard to read. The question is whether the y=315 line from M14 actually lands on that vertical or just crosses over it.

I'm checking how the wire at x=576 joins the M14 line at y=315, which I think is a dot connection rather than a crossing. If that holds, M4's source sits on the same net as M14's drain and M3's drain, so the pipeline's M10 source (net12) should be merged into net10.

I'm checking the M15 source against net16, and whether its gate ties to ground through the M6 and M7 gate node near x=654, though the wire near the bottom line is hard to trace.

I'm checking the M12 gate, which seems to tie down to a bias line at y=440 that runs toward the M13 source, though I can't yet tell whether that line reaches ground.

I'm checking the M13 drain, which should tie to the R1 bottom node at (40,352), not to ground, since the pipeline currently lists it as GND.

I'm checking the R1 negative terminal, which the pipeline ties to GND, against the drain node of M12 at (40,352). It looks like that node should be a new net rather than ground, with the drain and R1's negative side both on it.

I'm working out whether the M12 gate actually ties down to the y=440 line or just sits on the drain node at (40,352) with the M13 gate. The dot near (105,400) is the part I can't settle yet, since tying the gate to ground wouldn't make sense for this device.

I'm trying to reconcile the M12 gate with the y=440 line, which looks like it runs to ground, though the dot at (105,400) makes that unclear. I'm also weighing whether the pipeline's GND labels on the M13 gate and the M16/M15 gates are correct, since the ground assignments don't seem to match the image.

I'm checking whether the y=440 line really runs to ground at the M6 source, since the hop at x=576 makes that unclear. The M6/M7 gate tie at x=654 doesn't seem to connect to anything else I can see.

I'm treating the y=440 line as a bias net, not ground: it runs from the M12 gate across to the M6 and M7 gates, hopping over the ground leads. That means the R1 negative terminal, the M13 drain, and its gate all belong on that same bias net.

I'm checking the pipeline's M14 against the image's M13, which I think means its gate should sit on the bias net and its source should be ground rather than net14. The pipeline's M13 gate and drain both read GND, so I'm now treating them as the bias net, since they're the same device as the image's M12 and its drain ties to R1's negative side.

I'm now treating the bias net B as the node joining R1's negative side, the M13 drain and gate, and the gates of M14, M15, and M16, so those gate and drain labels that currently read GND need to change. I'm also checking that the M16 drain net8 matches the M2 drain and M5 source, and that M11's gate net10 is shared with M4's gate.

I'm checking whether the wire at x=654 runs from the M4/M5 gate node up to the M8/M9 gate line, or whether the dot at (654,274) is the only real junction. I'm not yet sure how the M4 gate reaches the y=340 area, so I'll leave that connection open for now.

Setting net13 to ground, since the image shows C1's bottom plate tied down. Then merging M10's source net12 into net10, and checking the M8/M9 gate net against M7's drain so the remaining net assignments line up.

I'm updating the net assignments now: M1's drain goes to net2, net12 folds into net10, and R1's negative side, along with the M13 drain and gate, moves onto a new bias net. The M14 gate also moves to that bias net, with its source going to ground, and the M15 and M16 gates follow the same bias net.
